`all` is an alias defined on the server and not in the client. Any resource can be added themselves to these aliases, or rather categories, see here for CRDs:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/582c4ebe267020ed59c1553b95c8ecc3e8b88c1a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/types.go#L247-L249

Although, before you open a PR to add anything to all, I can already warn you not to do it. See https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-cli/kubectl-conventions.md#rules-for-extending-special-resource-alias---all and probably a couple of places where this was tried and rejected. `all` is wrong, b/c it can differ from cluster to cluster, I'd encourage for you to define something like `networks` or something similar which will allow you to group all network releated resources. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95603 for how we defined `api-extensions` to encompass all of API extensions bits. That's the overall recommendation.

@soltysh So, the process of defining something like networks to group all network related resources will be similar to how you introduced api-extensions category in k8s apiserver. In that case you added k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/rest but what will be in case for adding network policies.
